title: Targeted Extraction using `id` and `class_`
instructions: From a mock product listing, extract the main title using its `id`, and then find all product names using their `class`.
steps: Use the `id` argument in `soup.find()` to extract the text from the element with `id="main-title"` and print it.
Use the `class_` argument in `soup.find_all()` to find all elements with `class="product-name"`. Store them in `product_names`.
Loop through `product_names` and print the text content of each.

solution:
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html_doc = """

Daily Deals on Electronics

Laptop X

Mouse Pro

Monitor 4K

""" # 1. Initialize BeautifulSoup soup = BeautifulSoup(html_doc, 'html.parser') # 2. Find and print the main title main_title = soup.find(id='main-title') print(f"Main Title: {main_title.text}") # 3. Find all product names by class product_names = soup.find_all(class_='product-name') # 4. Print all product names for name in product_names: print(name.text)
hints: To search by `id`, use the `id='value'` keyword argument in `find()`.
To search by `class`, use the `class_='value'` keyword argument in `find_all()`.
